en: A Liturgical Text for Paying Homage and Praising the Patriarchs of the Southern Mountain, composed by the Śramaṇa Renyue of Xiachuan.
I humbly observe that while the five vehicles have been set in motion, the śrāvakas were the very first; and as the radiance of the Tripiṭaka has spread, the Vinaya serves as its foundation.

One must strive to follow the True Dharma and truly belong to the lineage of the Patriarchs. Since China and India have shared a common script, the sages and worthies have followed one another’s footsteps.

I reverently contemplate the Master of Mount Nanshan, the Vinaya Master of Ximing Monastery. His traces appeared during the Sui and Tang dynasties, and his transformation spread throughout the capital and the surrounding lands.

As a model for Bodhisattvas, he manifested through three lifetimes; in promulgating the eternal precepts, he caused the *Dharmaguptaka-vinaya* (Four-Part Vinaya) to circulate. Having humbly reflected upon this...

With hempen cloth for robes and ink-stained brushes, he edited and supplemented [the texts] into finished chapters. Although the *mao* grass descended from the sky was divided, the *guānhuá* flowers upon his desk were not scattered.
Moved by his utmost sincerity, the divine responses were manifold. He met with celestial eloquence in conversation and employed divine power as his personal guard.
Thus, his virtue was ranked foremost among monks, making him a *Bhāṣita* (Upāli) for future generations; his learning was so abundant that he was truly a patriarch of the Confucian school.
As for the elder brother Pingshu of the Bao clan, the karmic conditions of the various regions have come to an end, and he has ascended to the realm of Heaven to serve as its successor.

Thus, he has attained wondrous functions that are immeasurable, beyond the reach of ordinary sentiments. We, having been fortunate enough to inherit the lineage of our ancestors and receive the counsel of our descendants, find ourselves at this approaching anniversary of his passing.

I venture to present this *yue* offering, contemplating the breeze of your compassion as if you were truly present. I have briefly composed these words of praise, hoping that you may partake of my sincerity and deign to turn your radiant gaze toward me.
With single-minded devotion, I invoke the Master of the Southern Mountain, Great Master Chengzhao, the Teacher of the Doctrine.
I pray that you will descend to this place of practice and accept my offerings.
When the moon is in the vast void, the reflections appear in a hundred rivers; when the mind merges with the Ultimate Way, forms manifest throughout the three realms.
Your virtue is as lofty as Mount De, surpassing the sages of antiquity; the river of your eloquence flows forth, nourishing those who study under you.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate before the Venerable Master Nanshan, who sought the śarīra within the precious casket at the Riyang Jingśe Monastery.
(All subsequent entries shall follow this pattern. Śīla wishes to receive the śarīra at the sacred altar; he first seeks it from the holy image.
With uplifted heads and hollowed hearts, they remained in profound stillness; A jeweled casket and pearl-like relics descended with a resonant sound.
The merit of Dharmaratna’s bringing them here was no different [from before]; Senghui’s prayer for their arrival may be considered the same.
The five-part body of the Buddha was thus formed from this; The Master’s transmission of the precepts was never bestowed in vain.
Therefore, with a single mind, I take refuge in and pay homage to him. (The following are all modeled after this.
With a single mind, I pay homage to the body of [Master] Zhuma of the Āraṇya when he was composing the *Vinaya-shichao*.
The Vinaya section was translated and transmitted during the Yao Qin dynasty; The lectures of the masters of the Yuan Wei era have arrived.
Though the ceremonial fans of the leaders are raised, The "coiled-script" [inscriptions] must ultimately await the brush of Nanshan.
Only when the five vehicles are yoked together can the path of the *vinaya* proceed; Only when the three practices penetrate in secret can the gate of liberation be reached.
Eliminating excess to transmit the true meaning without deception—where now are the new chapters and old commentaries?
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the body that practiced the *pratyutpanna-samādhi* within Mount Taiyi.
Selecting a site and divining a dwelling, he relied on a precious geomantic formation; Relying on the sutras to cultivate samādhi, he was known as the practitioner of the *Pratyutpanna-samādhi*.
The ninety-day retreat was completed at the site of the practice hall; When the samādhi was perfected, the nature of the mind was revealed.
Whether listening to the Dharma or encountering a dragon transformed into a woman, He manifested auspicious signs, once moving a lotus to bloom upon dry land.
Surveying the history of the Sangha among the sages and saints, one finds few whose diligence is like this.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the Cloud Chamber of the Qin lineage, who moved the celestial boys to serve him in his lifetime.
Long maintaining pure karma free from all defilement, He thus inspired a youth to attend his four modes of conduct.
Incense smoke swirls thickly from the corners of his seat; His tattered robes are elegant as he descends from the celestial realm.
Finding his own fulfillment in the secluded retreat, he wanders toward the realm of non-being; Who can know his unmoving mind as it strikes the silence?
The traces left by later generations may still be sought; the white clouds and empty chamber remain as they were of old.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate before the Western Ming Golden Temple and offer worship to the Buddha’s tooth relic, the very body that received offerings.
The Lord of the World entered nirvana, cremated by fire; His tooth-relics were distributed throughout the celestial palaces.
Were it not for the Bodhisattvas manifesting their sublime influence, How could Nala have transmitted this supreme treasure?
The tinkling of his pendants suddenly fell silent with the celestial music; Yet the colored light still bears the chill of the moon’s brilliance.
At that time, entering the stupa and submitting to the net of texts, may this forever serve as a source of merit and benefit for those in the toil of worldly life.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate before the precious ground of the Pure Official, who expounds the *Laṅkāvatāra* and the *Vinaya* while manifesting his physical body.
With a compassionate and dignified countenance, he sat upon the teacher’s seat; a multitude of true companions gathered at the assembly.
At the beginning, he expounded the Mahayana as the core of the sutras; in the end, through his study of the Vinaya, he established enduring models.
How could he begrudge dwelling among a thousand trees of jujubes? How could he be constrained by the counting sticks of a single room in transforming sentient beings?
With unimpeded eloquence beyond compare, you are worthy of receiving the nectar-bestowal from the Southern Heaven;
with single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Compassionate One at the Jinguan Monastery, who manifested his body during the time of the translations by Nadi.
A man from afar, admiring the Way, came to the land of Tang; The Great Being, receiving imperial grace, attended the translation assembly.
Seeking out the obscure, he co-translated the texts of the Five Indias; Unfolding his brilliance, he naturally topped the prefaces to the Three Sutras.
The roar of the Pu-lao bell resounded through the Pure Prohibitions; The fragrance of the *campaka* flower reached the Purple Palace.
As the Semblance Dharma gradually declines over a thousand years, who shall open and expound the jeweled cases and gilded scrolls?
With single-minded prostration for the sake of pure karma, I establish a precious altar at this temple at the time of receiving the precepts.
Where ancient Buddhas once consecrated the earth, the golden garden still stands as the altar was built;
five tiers of pearls connect like the shape of an inverted cauldron, and the four sides correspond to the pattern of the celestial sphere.
Success has been achieved, so those with long eyebrows come to pay their respects; those who increase their precepts continue to ascend as white-footed ones.
The one person who brilliantly expounded the Vinaya—this Indian monk was no mere empty praise;
with single-minded devotion I prostrate before his altar at Zhongnan, where he entered nirvana, his physical body remaining fixed and sealed.
In the realm of Yama, the traces of his manifestation have ended; In this auspicious month, he sat cross-legged in samādhi, never to return.
Though it is said that firewood and flames have a time of extinction, The flowers in the void were originally of the nature of non-arising.
Amidst the thorny forest, the celestial fragrance remains empty; Deeply sealed within the stone chamber, the night scene stretches long.
His virtue of precepts was ever more manifest after his passing, and Emperor Yizong posthumously conferred upon him the title "Chengzhao" (Illuminating Clarity).
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Honored One who was reborn in the Inner Court of Tuṣita Heaven during his final incarnation.
Having long cultivated the six perfections and the practice of contentment, And having closely attended the body of Amitābha through the two adornments,
Your physical remains have already been left behind in the Southern Mountains; Now, having received birth within the lotus womb in the Inner Court,
You have realized the nature of perfected reality (*pariniṣpanna-svabhāva*)— Yet, throughout the human realm, you never forget your heart to draw others upward.
With divine ears, I hear the sounds of lamentation; may I be among the first to attain liberation at the Dragon Flower Assembly.

With a sincere heart, I repent for myself and all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm of the ten directions: from the beginningless source of delusion, though originally pure and true, we have formed karmic bonds.
Though clarity has become my mindfulness, I have inhaled the dust of the phenomenal world to form toil. My forms flow through the seven realms of existence, with no place of return known;
the Three Vehicles reach out to all beings, yet there has never been a time for me to mount their carriage. Drifting along with delusions and karma, I am solitary and exposed amidst birth and death.

By virtue of subtle goodness from past conditions, I have now received this most precious spirit. Though I have shaved my hair and altered my appearance, I have already joined the Jewel of the Sangha.
Having severed worldly passions and washed away desires, I have yet to enter the stream of the Dharma. How could I have encountered the teachings of Zhongnan during this degenerate age?

I am ashamed that my body and mind harbor no firm resolve and that my nature is difficult to restrain. I violate the three thousand dignified deportments and breach the eighty thousand subtle precepts;
I repeatedly transgress the eternal statutes, and all wholesome dharmas have utterly perished. To cast my corpse among the waves and shallows—how could it endure even a single night?
How could one smell the fragrance of sandalwood from a carving made of excrement? It is only by relying on the Buddha’s compassionate concern that we are permitted to repent.

Since the provisional gate has now been opened, the true Way may be followed in common. One should contemplate that the nature of sin is empty and fluid, whereby the root of the precepts becomes pure once more;
thus the Four Reliances remain present and the Three Jewels are eternally real. We pray only that you will look upon us with pity and extend your protective mindfulness to all.
Having finished the repentance, take refuge with a sincere heart and pay homage with the crown of the head (all subsequent sections follow this pattern).
With a sincere heart,

I entreat the Tathāgatas to remain in the world for the sake of the Tripiṭaka, and I pray that the various patriarchs who have entered into the profound stillness throughout the ten directions will likewise remain.
I now entreat you to expound the Vinaya, To lead humans and devas for long to practice the Noble Path.
With a sincere heart, I rejoice in the equality of the One Vehicle; May all be granted hereafter at Vulture Peak, So that myriad virtues may together return to the Secret Treasury.
Therefore, the practitioner-bodhisattva, through causes, rejoices in all conditioned and untainted dharmas;
with a sincere heart,
they dedicate these toward the realization that self, Buddha, and sentient beings share the same essence, adorning one another with precepts, meditation, and wisdom.
Dedicating all merit toward Bodhi, Not dwelling in the flow of existence, they ascend to the other shore;
With a sincere heart they make vows,
wishing to uphold the Vinaya like the Foremost One, And personally proclaim the Perfect Penetration within the Dharma assembly.
"Body and mind are stilled and extinguished, attaining freedom from doubt.
These words of praise for the virtues of Dharma Master You of Xi River were composed by Dharma Master Gushan.
Originally, they did not appear in the ancestral ritual manuals; since they have already been adopted [into the liturgy], I have not altered them.
Eulogy for the Patriarchs of the Southern Mountain (Concluded)
